question: vsetvli-insert-zve64f.mir is a NEW upstream test at 20 (added by d2b8acc10464, did not exist at llvmorg-19.1.7, so it was never PASS at port-19-green; lit_diff mislabels it). Its input MIR hardcodes the INLINEASM operand flag 3145737, which encodes register class ID 47 (flag>>16 = 48 = RCID+1). In upstream 20 class 47 is VR; in the fork, the two fork register classes PulpV2 (v2i16) and PulpV4 (v4i8) in RISCVRegisterInfo.td (cluster codegen-core, present since step 18) sort among the 32-bit classes and shift every later ID by +2, so ID 47 is FPR64 and llc prints the comment '/* reguse:FPR64 */' instead of '/* reguse:VR */'. The fork's actual vsetvli-insertion output is identical to upstream (the test passes when only that comment text is substituted). The pass under test is run alone (-run-pass=riscv-insert-vsetvli), so the open 19 escalation about fork pre-RA passes being placed before RISCVInsertVSETVLI is NOT involved. The only resolutions are (a) a changed test expectation/input (forbidden for a worker; a test-regen could not fix it with update_mir_test_checks either, because the input MIR's hardcoded ID is itself the problem), or (b) removing the fork's PulpV2/PulpV4 register classes and adding v2i16/v4i8 to GPR the way upstream later does for the P extension (llvmorg-23: GPR carries XLenVecI8VT/XLenVecI16VT, no separate classes), which is a fork redesign (deleting fork register classes) that AGENT_RULES says must be escalated. Owner decision: accept this test as a known fork-induced expected failure (register-class-ID skew, no behaviour change), or schedule the PulpV2/PulpV4 -> GPR redesign (best at step 23 following upstream's P-extension packed-type model)?
